prompt.content:
You are coordinating a bimanual household robot through an evening chore run. Its two arms, "left" and "right", carry different end-effectors, so the SAME task can take a different number of minutes depending on which arm does it. Finish all chores as early as possible.

Chores (durations in minutes; "-" means none; bimanual and machine tasks have one fixed duration, shown in both columns):
  task              | type     | left_min | right_min | stations      | after                  
  sort_laundry      | arm      | 1        | 2         | -             | -                      
  load_washer       | arm      | 2        | 3         | washer        | sort_laundry           
  washer_cycle      | machine  | 8        | 8         | washer        | load_washer            
  transfer_to_dryer | arm      | 2        | 3         | washer,dryer  | washer_cycle           
  dryer_cycle       | machine  | 11       | 11        | dryer         | transfer_to_dryer      
  fold_bedsheet     | bimanual | 6        | 6         | folding_table | dryer_cycle            
  stow_linens       | arm      | 3        | 4         | -             | fold_bedsheet          
  scrape_batch_1    | arm      | 2        | 1         | -             | -                      
  rinse_batch_1     | arm      | 3        | 4         | sink          | scrape_batch_1         
  load_rack_1       | arm      | 2        | 1         | dishwasher    | rinse_batch_1          
  scrape_batch_2    | arm      | 1        | 2         | -             | -                      
  rinse_batch_2     | arm      | 3        | 2         | sink          | scrape_batch_2         
  load_rack_2       | arm      | 3        | 2         | dishwasher    | rinse_batch_2          
  dishwasher_cycle  | machine  | 9        | 9         | dishwasher    | load_rack_1,load_rack_2
  sweep_floor       | arm      | 2        | 3         | -             | -                      
  water_plants      | arm      | 5        | 4         | -             | -                      
  wipe_counters     | arm      | 4        | 3         | -             | -                      
  tidy_shelf        | arm      | 5        | 4         | -             | -                      

Task types:
- arm: needs exactly ONE arm — you choose which. The time charged is the CHOSEN arm's column.
- bimanual: needs BOTH arms simultaneously for its duration.
- machine: an appliance cycle. It needs NO arm and runs in parallel with anything else EXCEPT its listed station(s), which it occupies for its whole duration. You must still schedule its start time.

Scheduling rules:
1. Integer-minute grid: a task started at minute s with duration d occupies every resource it needs (arms and stations) for minutes s, s+1, ..., s+d-1 and finishes at s+d. Worked example: a 3-minute task started at minute 4 runs minutes 4, 5, 6 and finishes at 7; a successor may start AT minute 7.
2. Precedence is finish-to-start: a task may start only at or after the finish time of EVERY task in its "after" column (a predecessor's finish = its start + its CHOSEN arm's duration).
3. Each arm does one thing at a time; a bimanual task occupies BOTH arms. Arms may sit idle.
4. Stations (sink, dishwasher, washer, dryer, folding_table) have capacity 1 and are exclusive: a task occupies EVERY station it lists for its whole duration; a task listing two stations holds both at once.
5. Start times are integers from 0 to 79.
6. Schedule every one of the 18 tasks exactly once; entries may be listed in any order.

Arm labels: "left" or "right" for arm tasks (your choice), "both" for bimanual tasks, "none" for machine tasks. Example entries: ["load_washer", "left", 0] / ["fold_bedsheet", "both", 31] / ["washer_cycle", "none", 5].

Objective: MINIMIZE THE MAKESPAN — the latest finish time over all tasks. Warning: greedily starting the longest available chore first is NOT optimal here; the short tasks that unlock appliance cycles usually matter more.

Respond with your final answer as JSO
